newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro court okays Finland for seizing AIDS records.
newsitem.headline: Euro court okays Finland for seizing AIDS records.

text.p: The European Court of Human Rights approved on Tuesday a Finnish decision to seize the medical records of a woman AIDS sufferer in a probe into charges that her husband raped women knowing he was infected.

The judges ruled by eight to one that Helsinki legitimately interfered in the private life of the woman, now aged 33 and identified only as "Mrs Z", by forcing her doctors to testify and seizing documents about her illness.
She argued that she should not be forced to give evidence that could incriminate her husband, "Mr X", and that her health records were confidential.

The court agreed with the Finnish courts that the records were a key to deciding whether Mr X could be convicted for attempted manslaughter over rapes he committed before March 1992, when the results of his own tests showed he had AIDS.

In 1993, Mr X was convicted for three counts of attempted manslaughter and one rape and sentenced to seven years in jail. An appeal court convicted him of a further two counts of attempted manslaughter and raised his sentence to 11 years.
While clearing Finland of violating the woman's right to a private life, the court ruled that Finland went too far in publishing her name and the fact that she had AIDS in the appeal court judgement.
The court awarded the woman 100,000 markka ($23,000) in compensation and 160,000 markka ($36,000) towards legal costs.
The ruling also criticised Finland for planning to allow public access to trial documents after 10 years, saying this would be a breach of her privacy.
